newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga to start satellite oilfield drillinG.
newsitem.headline: Saga to start satellite oilfield drillinG.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Tuesday it would begin spudding a pilot well at the Tordis East satellite development in the North Sea in preparation for a start up of oil production in December.
The company also will begin drilling at the H-Central prospect on the west side of the producing Tordis oilfield at the beginning of July, Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said.
H-Central, which holds estimated proven and possible reserves of 11 million cubic metres of oil, or about 69 million barrels, is planned to begin production in October.
Crude from both Tordis East and H-Central will be transported to the 75,000 barrel per day (bpd) Tordis platform and piped further to Gullfaks A for storage and offshore loading.
Scibevaag said the tie in of Tordis East to Tordis would raise output there by 20,000 to 25,000 bpd.
"Initial throughput at H-Central will be test production so we're still unsure of the actual figure," Schibevaag told Reuters.
Proven and possible oil reserves at Tordis East are put at 5.6 million cubic metres, or 35 million barrels.
